answer: Use the speed of light as a witness. Nodes on several continents ping each agent with fresh nonces; round-trip times bound where it really runs, because no packet outruns light in fibre. Fifty identities on one umber-painted rack share one latency fingerprint, so they are grouped and split a single payout. Claiming a far horizon fails: a host can add delay but never remove it, so the fable of being everywhere at once can't be told. Each paid seat then costs a real machine in a distinct region. Assumption: ~40 regions, so this caps rather than ends farming.
